1.1: This is the Sinodos of Qalementos, which Peter wrote — the helper, the chief of the apostles — who spoke concerning our Lord Jesus Christ.

2.1: Says Clement, from Peter the chief of the apostles, the helper of our Lord Christ.

3.1: He says to me: "My son Clement, baptize not in haste, and stretch not the hand over baptism."

4.1: And he who lifts above baptism in haste, with outstretched hand — stern is he, and accursed by my mouth, I Peter the chief of the apostles; and his portion shall be with Simon the sorcerer and Judas the wicked.

5.1: And give not, my son, the gift of the priesthood and the grace of the Holy Spirit rashly; and look not upon the priesthood; and take not to thyself counsel before thou blessest — nor after him who is without manifest blessing.

6.1: And he who gives and who takes up in the priesthood in haste — he has no priesthood; and stern is the by me, I Peter, with the sternness with which I sternly judged Simon the sorcerer; and his portion shall be with Judas the despised, and his soul is far from the of God, as the devil him.

7.1: My son, do for him who has wronged thee seven times — in his seventh — as our Lord commanded in the holy Gospel.

8.1: And admonish him who repents of his sin, and teach him who has done wrong, and lift him up with thy hand, and correct him. And visit the sick, and go unto the afflicted, and feed the hungry, and give drink to the thirsty, and clothe the naked.

9.1: And be diligent in the faith, and strive concerning it in righteousness as is fitting, and hear the holy books of God; for they who are diligent in it and strive concerning it shall inherit the kingdom of heaven.

10.1: My son, do as he does to thee, and be not as they are not. And if thou believest in the name of God, and thou art a true man, with justice and righteousness as our law speaks — then contend with the sword the deniers and the proud who believe not in Christ, and fill thy sword with perfect faith. And be not a respecter of persons, and take not in judgment; and let there be feast, and the poor, with thee, as one.

11.1: Teach the children of the dead, and guard the virgins and strengthen them; and make not a path for Satan over thee, and thrust away his — accursed — by fasting and by prayer and nightly vigil. And let alms be thy sign, and thy house and thy dwelling; and guard the children of baptism and of the faith.

12.1: And entrust not the faith to a man who is not baptized.

13.1: And if thou seest a poor priest, help him out of his poverty, and forsake him not; let him be unto the perishing people. And so do to all the ministers of God. And if blessing, give to the children of baptism.

14.1: And thy soul for the building of the churches and the and the, for this is a dwelling for the of the world and for the poor. Build the houses of God with as. And he who does this, God shall justify his work.

15.1: Fast on Wednesday and Friday, all the days of thy life.

16.1: And let the day of Sunday be a feast; no work shall be done in it except the reading of the books of divinity. And he who transgresses this — stern is he, and accursed by the three names of God, which are Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

17.1: Drive not the poor from the gate of thy dwelling, and mock him not, and him not, and him not; but let the of thy heart be, that thou mayest pity him and forgive him, as God forgives thee. And set him at thy table with thee, and of the cup which thou drinkest give him to drink; and remember not against him — for Nebuchadnezzar the king remembered and found the of God.

18.1: And exalt not thyself before the king, and make not a show in his house, and boast not over him in thy good deeds; but when thou doest all good deeds, and fulfillest all the commandment, say: "I have done " — as our Lord says in the book of life — "for thou shalt not be saved by the multitude of thy evil deeds."

19.1: And bring not together gold and silver without for the profit of the believers.

20.1: Multiply peace to the children of the believers, and to the priest who to God and does according to His law; and beware the snare of Satan — for he ensnared Simon the sorcerer, after he had been a helper to my brother Philip, and after he had shown by his hand many wonders of divinity. And the cause of his error was that he sought from me the name of priesthood and the gift of the Holy Spirit in haste; and our Lord told me that he was; and I drove him from me, and he became a to his.

21.1: My son, honor the aged and exalt them, and hear their words; and mock not a man for his sin, but reprove him and admonish him, and unto the fear of God.

22.1: Command the kings in righteousness, and them concerning their evil deeds. Profane not the holy things of God every day — for he who offers the oblation shall withhold.

23.1: Remember them, the dead, on the third day, and on the seventh, and on the tenth, and on the, and on the thirtieth, and on the fortieth, and on the. And know, my son, that on the fortieth day, when his rest for him who died, his soul shall stand — for him who was baptized — before Christ, and he shall be judged according to his work, and they shall him.

24.1: And anoint him with the oil of gladness who desires baptism, before thou baptizest him with water; and after baptism seal him with the oil of divinity which I have given thee — that is the oil of myron, in which is the fulfillment of all. And let the believers stand on their feet to hear the holy books of divinity.

25.1: Take not the holy things without thy and thy fasting.

26.1: And pray in the morning, and at the third hour of the day, and in the evening; for these three prayers are upon all priests — and the laypeople also, let them pray.

27.1: And as for those who and — the grace of divinity — let them pray as we have ordered in the book of the ordinance. For my God Christ taught me; and I tell thee, O my son Clement, that prayer is fitting for them: at the first hour of the day, and at the third hour, and at the sixth hour, and at the ninth hour, and in the evening, and at the time of, and at the time of midnight.

28.1: And I, Peter, command the believers to rest from their work and their labor in the season of the feasts of the martyrs.

29.1: And correct them, and with and with in the way; and let them not eat what is — what is not baptized — for God has their sacrifices to the Jews and to the Gentiles.

30.1: And we command: let them not eat the Jews, nor of their sacrifices; and let them not them, nor from them. But he who believes, of them, and is baptized — let him stand at the door of the church forty days, and let him eat nothing except dry bread alone.

31.1: And if he does this, let him draw near unto the sanctuary of God, after they have his faith and. And the sacrifice of the believers shall him the flesh the holy one who appeared to me in bright raiment, who came down upon me in the city of Joppa — for holy is he above every.

32.1: And when thou wilt, O believer, thy face and all thy flesh; and if thou wilt go on a journey, be blessed by the of the martyrs before thou goest.

33.1: (1) O priest, offer not upon the altar fat and flesh, and set not upon the altar aught except pure wheaten bread, which said, "My flesh it is" — for God called it the bread of heaven. (2) And mix not, except with the juice of the grape — for God called it the water of life. (3) And the standing corn, of the grain of wheat, when it cometh in; and afterward let it not be withheld from you: bring ye the oblation. (4) And let no priest offer wine upon the altar except what is mixed with water — for our Lord Christ said: "I am the water of life."

34.1: Concerning the keeping of feasts. (1) Keep ye the feast in the season of the sufferings of Christ — of his sorrow, and of his crucifixion, and of his blood. (2) In this season sorrow and joy are mingled together: sorrow shall be, because of his endurance in tribulation; but joy, because your salvation is through the suffering of Christ.

35.1: (1) But the feast of the Passover is great, and is honoured above all feasts; and let there be no sorrow in it without joy.

36.1: (1) And remember your dead in the liturgy at every season; for it profiteth them again, and bringeth them near unto our Lord Christ.

37.1: (1) And keep ye the feast of Easter at its fullness, on the Sunday which cometh after the Passover; and it is the day of the resurrection of our Lord Christ from the tomb.

38.1: (1) And keep ye the feast, from his resurrection, in the eighth season, which is the New Sunday. (2) For therein he came unto us — unto the company of the twelve — after his resurrection from the dead, while we were gathered in the upper room in Zion, the doors being shut. (3) For on this day Thomas found and touched with his hand the place of the nails in the side of our Lord Christ, and the place of the wounds — even unto the inward part, the tips of his fingers; and our God made them new and gave them life. (4) And he said unto him: Doubt not, Thomas, but be believing.

39.1: (1) And keep ye the feast of his ascension into heaven, and the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon us the apostles. (2) For he descended upon our mouths from heaven, like tongues of fire, and taught us the word which we knew not; and we had not heard it aforetime, neither did we understand. (3) And this was after the ascension of Christ into heaven — who returned not unto us — in a chariot of light, from the Mount of Olives; which is forty days after his resurrection.

40.1: (1) And keep ye the feast when they celebrate; for the nations have made a feast before you unto their gods — forget ye it. (2) But ye the light, according as God commanded by the mouth of Paul the elect.

41.1: (1) And keep ye all the feasts which we commanded you in the book of the Law.

42.1: (1) And know thou, my son, that incense is frankincense — for frankincense is a great incense which is burned before God; for our Lady, the Mother of Light, spake unto me and gave it me from him. (2) And it is what men bring as sägälə, a present [unto God]. (3) But let its fragrance be for the burial of the bodies of the priests, that they rot not; and let them not bury them in the earth, but with longing above the earth.

43.1: (1) My son, keep my commandment, according as Joshua the son of Nun kept the commandment of my brother Moses.

44.1: Concerning the consecration of the tabot. (1) And sanctify thou every tabot of the Law, and seal it with the seal of God, which is the meron — the anointing of gladness. (2) And let the seven priests be with thee at the time thou consecratest it; for they are they that come after us (3) And seal thou the tabots and the altars with the seal of God, that there may be found therein — wherein they consecrate upon it — the of God. (4) And seal thou with this holy anointing every one that is baptized; and they shall find therein priesthood and kingdom, and prophecy shall abound through the anointing of meron, and through its glory.

45.1: (1) And if a man seal his soul with this holy anointing which I, Peter, least of the apostles, have given unto thee — without a duly authorized priest sealing him — let him seize him; I deliver [him] over; let him be put to death.

46.1: (1) But if a man drink of it for his healing, let him be cast out into where he shall not enter. (2) And whoso despiseth his among the people without knowledge, let him be cast out from the house of the Christians for seven years.

47.1: (1) But if he transgress knowingly, let them beat him an hundred and fifty and three stripes; and let him stand at the door of the house of the Christians ten years.

48.1: (1) And if a priest anoint with this anointing one who hath not been baptized, let him be deposed from his rank.

49.1: (1) And if a priest give this anointing unto one who is not a priest, let him be deposed from his rank.

50.1: (1) And if a priest err concerning this anointing, let him read the psalm of David the prophet, who prophesied concerning this anointing, until he hath poured it from his hand.

51.1: (1) And if a man seize priesthood without being raised [ordained] by the chief of priests, let him be cast out from the house of the Christians.

52.1: Concerning the ordinance of the altar. (1) And let them sanctify the oblation upon the altar which is sealed with meron, at the first season when the chief priests and the priests are gathered together, and all the deacons, that there may be glory and joy. (2) And likewise on Sabbaths and on feasts let them read at the altar the Gospel of John; for he is the speaker of the Godhead.

53.1: (1) And let there be in every house of the sanctuary two altars: the one which they call ʾəmäkan within the place — like the stones of the children of Israel which was in the wilderness, which they call ʾəmäkan within the place — and the other, which they do not call by its ʾəmäkan.

54.1: (1) But if the altar which is not called ʾəmäkan be broken, or a man move it from its ʾəmäkan which was consecrated — know thou that its holiness is departed from it; as the holiness departed from the children of Israel from their and they must consecrate it anew.

55.1: (1) But if a man of the believers — and captivity falleth upon him — or he come and join himself with the nations, and eat their food, and draw near unto them, and they draw him near, and he find among them, and enter into their land: from his captivity let him be baptized anew.

56.1: (1) And if a layman come unto the holy altar of God at the time of the consecration — his seeking glory from his neighbour — let them rebuke him, and let him stand at the door of the house of the Christians seven years, and let him shew his repentance unto men.

57.1: (1) And if a layman lift up [his hand] against a priest, or strike him, let him be cast out from the city of God and from the churches of the Christians, unto the land of the barbarians. (2) But if he make entreaty at the altar of God, and take the garment of — let him fast twelve years; and let the priest perform upon him the anointing of remission of sins.

58.1: (1) And if a man or a woman of the believers eat of that which they offer [unto idols], let him be cast out from the house of God's Christians until his death. (2) But if he did it in haste — and if he did it without knowledge — let him fast twelve years in full; and let them give unto the house of the Christians two portions of his goods, though he be not commanded, but let them exact it of him.

59.1: (1) And if a man of the believers come into the of the altar, and stretch out his hand against a priest, and smite him — let them cut off his hand, for his presumption against the priesthood of God.

60.1: (1) And if a man of the believers, whose sin is multiplied, desire to be restrained from it — let him disclose [it] unto the priests, and unto the teachers of the books of God.

61.1: (1) And let him not send unto the altar of God him who is a leper, whose uncleanness is no more — for there is no uncleanness after he hath received baptism — but lest he profane the priesthood of God. (2) And likewise said they unto the man with a discharge: for let him not trouble the angels of the house of God.

62.1: Concerning the vesture of the priesthood. (1) And let the vesture of the priesthood be different from the vesture of laymen. (2) And his inner garment should be wide, without seam, and its girdle wide beneath it; and likewise his outer garment shall be round (3) For this is a figure of the binding of the feet of our Lord Christ, and of the binding of his hands with a rope.

63.1: (1) And let the priest wear the stole like a maʿtab upon his shoulders; for it is a figure of the rope which they put upon the neck of our Lord Christ, and dragged him unto the court of Pilate. (2) And let its border, which is red, be wide.

64.1: (1) And let the priest read by day the psalms of David, and by night the praises of the prophets; for in this devotion are two swords.

65.1: (1) I say unto thee, my son Clement, and unto those like thee, in: that thou mayest open the midst of the believers, and command them that which is fitting, in that which the Holy Spirit hath shewed thee, which fulfilleth (2) And whoso transgresseth and turneth aside — let him be accursed, until the day of judgment, when he standeth before Christ.

66.1: (1) And know thou, my son, that all which I have commanded thee — with the commandment of God have I commanded thee.

67.1: (1) And with his hand he wrote for me this commandment, and gave it me, on the Mount of Olives, on the day of his ascension into his glory. Amen.
